title: Friendship with Ferguson, reading, and Gennett records at Richmond, Indiana
summary: Pillars reads in the library, learns golf from Ferguson, and the band records 'Clementine' and 'I Found a New Baby' for Gennett.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: By all means. And that's the way it was. We played all through that territory and Mr. Ferguson became one of my best friends, he took me out -- the first golf ball I ever hit in my life, he taught me how to hold a club. C. Ferguson, A very fine person and a very smart business man.

We rehearsed almost everyday, that's all we had to do was just hang around and rehearse, and all my spare time was spent in the library, I would go to the library and read everyday. That was my hobby, just reading, reading. Trying to learn, trying to pick up this. Read, read, read. We had a chance to make some records for the Gennett people. And we drove up to Richmond, Indiana am I right, Charles?
We drove up to Richmond, Indiana and made the recordings; one was "Clementine" and one was "I Found A New Baby." Just two sides, am I right, Charles?
The two sides. The "Clementine" arrangement was arranged by Gus Wilson. We stayed there until late
Spring of '33. And then we accepted some bookings out east. Right Charles?
